pattern_description: Scammer contacts victim claiming a wrong/excess payment was made to them via UPI, and asks them to 'refund' it by clicking a link or scanning a QR code / entering UPI PIN. In reality, scanning a QR code or entering a PIN is only needed to RECEIVE money in some flows, but scammers exploit collect requests to drain the victim's account.
example_text: Sir, maine galti se aapke account mein 5000 rupees bhej diye hai. Please is QR code ko scan karke wapas kar dijiye. Turant kariye warna main police complaint karunga.
red_flags: Urgency/threat of police action
Request to scan QR code to 'return' money
Unknown sender claiming accidental transfer
Pressure to act immediately
source_citation: RBI Alert on UPI Fraud (RBI Consumer Awareness, 2023) - 'Never scan a QR code or share UPI PIN to receive money'
legit_contrast: Real refunds from banks/apps never require scanning a QR code or entering a PIN; PINs are only for sending money.

pattern_description: Fraudster impersonates police, CBI, customs, or narcotics officials via video/voice call, claims the victim's Aadhaar/phone number is linked to a crime (drugs, money laundering, courier with illegal items), and threatens 'digital arrest' unless the victim transfers money or stays on video call under surveillance.
example_text: This is Customs Department Mumbai. A parcel with your Aadhaar linked to illegal substances was intercepted. You are under digital arrest. Do not disconnect this call or inform anyone. Transfer funds for verification immediately.
red_flags: Claim of 'digital arrest' (not a real legal concept in India)
Threat of arrest without due process
Instruction not to hang up or contact family/lawyer
Demand for money transfer for 'verification' or 'clearance'
source_citation: CERT-In / Ministry of Home Affairs Cybercrime Advisory on Digital Arrest Scams (2024) - 'Digital arrest' is not a legal procedure under Indian law.
legit_contrast: No Indian law enforcement agency arrests, detains, or holds a citizen 'digitally' over video call, nor asks for money transfers to avoid arrest.

pattern_description: Message claims a package (often from abroad) is held at customs or a courier hub pending a small 'clearance fee' or 'customs duty', with a link to pay. The link leads to a phishing page that harvests card details or triggers a larger unauthorized debit.
example_text: Your parcel from India Post is on hold due to unpaid customs duty of Rs 39. Pay now to release: http://indiapost-delivery-verify.xyz/pay
red_flags: Non-official domain mimicking a real courier/postal brand
Small, plausible-sounding fee to lower suspicion
Urgency ('parcel will be returned')
Shortened or suspicious URL
source_citation: CERT-In Advisory on Courier/Delivery Phishing Scams
legit_contrast: India Post, FedEx, DHL, etc. do not collect customs duty via SMS links; duties are paid through official portals or at delivery.

pattern_description: Victim receives a job offer (often via WhatsApp) with unrealistically high pay for simple tasks (e.g., 'like YouTube videos', 'rate products online'), and is asked to pay a 'registration fee' or join a Telegram group where they are later asked to invest money for higher 'task rewards'.
example_text: Congratulations! You are selected for a part-time job. Earn Rs 3000-5000 daily by liking YouTube videos. Join our Telegram group to start: t.me/xxxxx. Registration fee Rs 500 only.
red_flags: Unrealistic pay for trivial work
Upfront registration/fee requirement
Redirect to Telegram/WhatsApp groups outside official channels
No formal interview or company verification process
source_citation: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) Advisory on Task-Based Job Fraud (2024)
legit_contrast: Legitimate employers do not ask candidates to pay money to get hired or to unlock 'task earnings'.

pattern_description: Message impersonates a bank claiming the victim's KYC has expired or account will be blocked/suspended unless they click a link to update details or call a number, leading to phishing pages or scammers who ask for OTP/PIN over call.
example_text: Dear Customer, your SBI account KYC has expired. Your account will be blocked in 24 hours. Update immediately: http://sbi-kyc-update.net/verify
red_flags: Non-bank domain (not endswith .sbi.co.in etc.)
Artificial urgency (24 hour deadline)
Request for OTP/PIN which banks never ask for
Grammar/formatting inconsistent with official bank communication
source_citation: RBI Guidelines - Banks never ask for OTP, PIN, or CVV via call/SMS/email
legit_contrast: Banks update KYC through branch visits, verified net-banking portals, or official apps, never via unsolicited SMS links.

pattern_description: Victim downloads an unauthorized instant-loan app that accesses their contacts/photos, then after taking a small loan, faces harassment, morphed images, and blackmail from recovery agents if repayment (often at very high hidden interest) is delayed.
example_text: Your loan of Rs 5000 is now due with a total of Rs 15000 including charges. Pay within 2 hours or we will send your photo to all your contacts.
red_flags: App not listed on RBI's registered NBFC list
Excessive interest/fees not disclosed upfront
Threats involving contacts or photos
No formal loan agreement or physical verification
source_citation: RBI Advisory on Unauthorized Digital Lending Apps (2022)
legit_contrast: RBI-registered lenders do not threaten borrowers with personal data exposure and must disclose all charges upfront.

pattern_description: Victim is told they've won a lottery, lucky draw, or prize (often referencing a well-known brand like KBC or a phone company) and must pay a 'processing fee' or 'tax' to claim it.
example_text: CONGRATULATIONS! Your number has won Rs 25,00,000 in the KBC Lucky Draw 2026. To claim, pay processing fee of Rs 4999 to this UPI ID: kbcwinner@upi
red_flags: You never entered a lottery you're being told you won
Requirement to pay to receive winnings
Use of a well-known brand name without official association
Payment via personal UPI ID rather than any official channel
source_citation: TRAI / Cyber Crime Awareness - Common Lottery Scam Pattern
legit_contrast: Legitimate lotteries or brand promotions never require winners to pay money upfront to release winnings.

pattern_description: Scammer builds a relationship on a matrimonial or dating platform, then invents an emergency (medical, travel, customs) requiring urgent money transfer, often after weeks of conversation without ever meeting in person.
example_text: My love, I am stuck at customs in Mumbai airport, they are asking for Rs 50,000 to release my luggage which has gifts for you. Please send urgently, I will pay you back when I land.
red_flags: Relationship never met in person despite claims of love
Sudden financial emergency
Requests routed through unusual payment channels
Inconsistent personal details/photos possibly reverse-searchable
legit_contrast: N/A - pattern-based; verified relationships rarely require emergency unsolicited money transfers so early.

pattern_description: Victim searches online for a bank/UPI app's customer care number and lands on a fake number, or scammer calls posing as support after a victim posts a complaint, then asks to install a remote-access app (AnyDesk/TeamViewer) 'to fix the issue', gaining full control of the device.
example_text: Sir I am calling from PhonePe support regarding your complaint. Please install AnyDesk app so I can fix your account issue remotely.
red_flags: Request to install remote access/screen sharing app
Contacted you rather than you calling verified support
Asks for app passcodes or lets them 'see' the screen with UPI PIN visible
source_citation: NPCI/CERT-In Advisory on Remote Access App Fraud
legit_contrast: Official bank/UPI support never asks customers to install remote-access screen-sharing apps.

category: SIM Swap / Fake Mobile Operator Scam
pattern_description: Victim receives a call/message posing as a telecom operator asking to press a number or share an OTP to 'upgrade SIM to 5G' or 'prevent SIM deactivation', which is actually a SIM-swap attempt to hijack their number for banking OTP access.
example_text: Dear customer, your SIM will be deactivated today due to KYC issue. Press 1 or share the OTP sent to you to keep your number active.
red_flags: Any request for OTP over call/SMS
Urgency about SIM deactivation
Instruction to press digits during a call from an unknown/spoofed number
source_citation: TRAI/DoT Advisory - Telecom operators never ask for OTP to keep SIM active
legit_contrast: Telecom providers do not deactivate SIMs via a single missed KYC step communicated by SMS/call with an OTP share request.
